conditions: f is real analytic on a connected open real interval containing a and x. The distance |x-a| is strictly less than the Taylor series radius of convergence at a; boundary equality is not asserted. The order-zero derivative is f itself.
spoken_aliases: f of x equals the sum from n equals zero to infinity of the product of the fraction with numerator the nth derivative of f evaluated at a and denominator n factorial and open parenthesis x minus a close parenthesis raised to the power n
f of x equals the sum from n equals zero to infinity of the nth derivative of f at a divided by n factorial times the quantity x minus a raised to the power n

evidence: Real analyticity near a gives a convergent power series equal to f near a. Termwise differentiation identifies coefficient n as f^(n)(a)/n!. The series defines a real-analytic function throughout its open convergence interval. On its intersection with the stated connected interval of analyticity, the real-analytic identity theorem extends equality from the neighborhood of a to x. No boundary equality is asserted.
